acceptance.schoolAuthorityAdmin: Production invitations, billing and administration retain their existing authorization, mandatory MFA, subscription and school-authority boundaries. No administrator account or subscription is changed as QA.
acceptance.schoolScopedAdmin: Existing school and role restrictions remain. No preview receives a credential that can elevate these permissions.
acceptance.transportationAdmin: Existing transportation permissions and billing denials remain. Production functions retain their original credential bytes.
acceptance.guardian: Production access remains limited to linked students. Personal consent, optional MFA, quiet hours and device permissions remain. Previews use synthetic responses and receive no production server credentials.
acceptance.driver: Production access remains limited to own or assigned operations. Personal consent, optional MFA and location permission remain. No trip, location fix or external notification is generated as QA.
acceptance.platformAdmin: Existing privileged authorization and MFA remain. Only the protected, exact-main workflow can apply this policy; encrypted recovery is uploaded before mutation. Netlify cloud builds are stopped while production keeps serving. Existing provider scopes and secret flags are retained on Free; credentials resolve only in production. Future artifacts are built and deployed through protected GitHub jobs. Previously secret-bearing unpublished previews are retired without deleting production deployments.
acceptance.channels: No notifications, invoices, charges, invitations or real recipient subscriptions are created as QA.
acceptance.failure: Refuse unknown or inherited credentials, unmanaged dev servers, unreadable all-context fallbacks, target drift or inventory overflow. After encrypted recovery is retained, stop Netlify cloud builds. Leave existing production value records untouched; create a production value only from a readable existing fallback and verify it before removing fallback/non-production context records. Preserve provider scopes and secret flags on Free. Never send masked strings as values or delete production records. On partial failure retain recovery and progress and leave cloud builds stopped. Never restore administrative credentials to previews. Recovery captures readable values and opaque provider references; it is not a complete external secret vault. Configuration and source-event acceptance remain separate.
